Where we are in the process. SEO moves in a set order: Google shows you more often, then it shows you higher, then the clicks follow. We are in the middle stage. Visibility and rankings are both improving; click volume is still small and is expected to build as positions move into the top few results. That is the normal shape of month one, and it is the honest position.

Visibility rose 20% between the two halves of the month, from 6,813 to 8,165 impressions. Average position improved from 10.4 to 9.7 — a modest but meaningful move, because position 10 is the bottom of page one and almost nobody looks at page two.

03 — Spam score

Spam score reduced from 8% to 1%

A spam score estimates how risky a website's incoming links look. Lower is better. A high score quietly holds back rankings across a whole site.

📉 Spam score over the reporting period
Start and current figures measured with Moz. Intermediate points show the direction of travel.

The site was carrying a spam score of 8% at the start of the month, largely from low-quality and irrelevant links built up over the years. We audited the full backlink profile, disavowed the harmful domains and cleaned up the weak listings. It now sits at 1%.

What we did

🔍 Link audit & disavow

  • Exported the full backlink profile from Moz, Semrush and Search Console
  • Scored every referring domain for spam risk
  • Identified links from link farms, adult, gambling and scraper sites
  • Built and submitted a disavow file to Google
  • Logged every link in a central tracking database

📂 Listings & citations

  • Audited every directory listing carrying a link
  • Removed listings on low-quality and abandoned directories
  • Merged duplicate listings splitting the business's authority
  • Corrected outdated contact details on third-party sites
  • Standardised name, address and phone across all listings

📡 Keeping it clean

  • Reviewed anchor text balance across the link profile
  • Set quality thresholds for all future link building
  • Set up alerts for newly detected harmful links
  • Established a monthly link profile review
  • Documented the full removal and disavow history

Why it matters. This work produces no immediate visible result, which is why it often gets skipped. But a clean link profile means every content page and every new link from here lands on a domain Google already trusts, rather than one it is quietly discounting.

The 21-year domain age is a genuine advantage that cannot be bought — Google gives weight to long, consistent trading history. The clear opportunity is the quality of the link profile: only 156 of roughly 2,000 links are rated high quality, which is what the ongoing link building is there to change.

Ongoing link building

We are building new quality links steadily across four channels — article submissions, social sharing, business directories and branded profiles. Every link is quality-checked before use and logged, so the spam score stays where it is now.

Realistic expectation. Backlinks compound slowly. Domain authority typically moves a few points over several months, not weeks. The aim is steady, safe growth rather than a fast spike — which is what caused the spam score problem in the first place.

The focus for next month

Almost all of the site's search visibility is currently carried by the homepage alone. The priority is dedicated service pages, each written around one service and one keyword group. The screen repair page is already written and ready to publish.

Realistically, new pages take 4 to 8 weeks to settle in Google after publishing. The aim for next month is more page-one positions and steady growth in visits — not an overnight jump.

09 — Plain English

The terms used in this report

ImpressionsHow many times the site appeared in Google results, whether clicked or not.
PositionWhere a page sits in results. 1 is the top; page one is roughly the top 10.
KeywordThe phrase a customer types into Google, e.g. "phone repair london".
BacklinkA link from another website to yours. Google treats it as a vote of confidence.
Spam ScoreAn estimate of how risky a site's links look. Lower is better.
Domain AuthorityAn industry score, 1–100, estimating a site's ranking power.
DisavowFormally telling Google to ignore specific harmful links.
Schema markupHidden code explaining your business to Google, enabling star ratings and FAQs.
SitelinksExtra page links Google shows under a result, awarded automatically.
Search ConsoleGoogle's free tool showing how a site performs in search.
